stem: Two records have unique IDs A and B. A currently belongs to Intake; B belongs to Review. Their IDs must be SWAPPED while each record keeps its department and all its incoming links. Local rule: a rename atomically changes an ID and every incoming link to that record; a rename is forbidden if its destination ID is already occupied. T is an unused temporary ID. Which ordered plan completes the swap and leaves T unused?
explanation: After A→T, Intake and its links use T, and A is vacant. B→A moves Review and its links into A, vacating B. T→B then moves Intake into B and vacates T. Renaming T→B before B is vacated collides at B; renaming B→T collides at T; ending with A→B moves Review back to B and strands Intake at T. All offered plans start with the same valid step, so later states determine the result.

stem: An office must staff Intake, Payments and Release in BOTH morning and afternoon. Each shift requires three DISTINCT workers. Skills: Neri—Intake or Payments; Oli—Payments or Release; Paz—Intake or Release; Quin—all three. Paz is absent in the morning; Neri is absent in the afternoon. Anyone working both shifts must change counters. Which complete plan works?

choices.text: Morning I:Neri, P:Oli, R:Quin; Afternoon I:Paz, P:Oli, R:Quin
Morning I:Neri, P:Oli, R:Quin; Afternoon I:Quin, P:Oli, R:Paz
Morning I:Neri, P:Oli, R:Quin; Afternoon I:Paz, P:Quin, R:Oli
Morning I:Quin, P:Neri, R:Oli; Afternoon I:Paz, P:Quin, R:Oli

explanation: In the valid plan, morning Neri/Oli/Quin cover Intake/Payments/Release and afternoon Paz/Quin/Oli cover Intake/Payments/Release. All are present and qualified. Both returning workers change counters: Oli moves Payments→Release and Quin moves Release→Payments. The plan that keeps afternoon Oli at Payments and Quin at Release repeats both counters; another repeats Oli at Payments; the plan starting morning Release with Oli repeats Oli at Release. Every alternative otherwise covers all counters with qualified available staff, so the cross-shift rule must be checked.

explanation: A must leave 10:00 so B can leave a later wave. C is not ready for 10:00 and requires 2 slots at 11:00; B adds 1 there. D therefore joins A at 10:00. Capacities are 3 and 3, and every release condition holds.

explanation: X contributes 250, Y contributes 0 after its latest cancellation, Z contributes 40 once, and W contributes −30. Net=260. Counting duplicate Z or retaining Y's earlier posted state gives the tempting incorrect totals.

stem: Custody transfers only on a receiving signature whose seal code matches the file. Transport alone has no effect; a mismatched code makes a signature invalid. Initially Ada holds P(seal 31) and Q(seal 42). P: Ben signs code 31 at 09:12; Cora signs code 13 at 09:19; Dino signs code 31 at 09:23. Q: Cora signs code 42 at 09:15; a messenger departs to return it to Ada at 09:18; Ada signs code 42 at 09:22. At 09:21, who has recorded custody of P and Q respectively?
explanation: For P, Ben's 09:12 signature is valid; Cora's 09:19 signature uses the wrong seal and cannot transfer custody; Dino's valid signature is still in the future. For Q, Cora's 09:15 signature is valid and Ada has not yet signed at 09:21. Thus Ben and Cora retain recorded custody. Both codes and the time boundary must be applied; mere transport does not transfer Q.

stem: Local retention: count 30 calendar days AFTER closure; closure day is day 0. Every day covered by a hold is excluded from this count. Hold start and release dates are BOTH excluded days. Disposal is allowed when 30 counted days have elapsed and no hold remains active. Today is 5 June 2027. P closed 6 May, no hold. Q closed 1 May, hold 11–15 May. R closed 1 May, hold 11–16 May. S closed 1 May, hold 11 May–5 June inclusive. Which COMPLETE list may be disposed of today?
explanation: P counts 7–31 May(25 days)+1–5 June(5)=30. Q counts 2–31 May(30) minus 5 held days, plus 5 June days=30. R excludes 6 held days, leaving 29; S is still held through today. Thus only P and Q qualify. Inclusive hold endpoints and exclusion of closure day both change borderline results.
